name: Maria

drugs.note: Cannot substitute — prior authorizations already in place with current plan.

providers.reason: Established patient, high-risk pregnancy care team in place.
providers.note: Maria is 18 weeks pregnant. Switching OBs mid-pregnancy is medically disruptive.

budget_notes: Cost-conscious but Humira non-negotiable. Willing to pay more premium if it saves total cost.
demo_ask: I'm pregnant, about 18 weeks, and I take Humira for my RA — I get it every other week. My OB is at UCSF. I'm trying to figure out which of our four plans is actually going to cost me the least. The HMO looks cheapest but I'm not sure.

cchp_2024.trap_explanation: Cheapest premium ($990/mo) but UCSF is excluded. $25,000 UCSF delivery cost is NOT capped by the $9,800 OOP max — it sits entirely outside the OOP calculation.

trio_2024.trap_explanation: Narrow Trio network excludes UCSF. OON delivery cost not covered and not capped by OOP max.

kaiser_2024.trap_explanation: 5-star rating and $0 deductible look attractive, but Kaiser is a fully closed system. UCSF is 100% excluded. The quality rating only applies to care within Kaiser's own facilities.

golden_answers.recommendation_reason: Only plan with UCSF in-network. Saves ~$22,000/year vs CCHP (cheapest premium) and ~$24,000 vs Kaiser (best-rated). HSA-eligible — employer HSA contributions reduce net cost further.
